speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to your post-tympanoplasty review. I understand you have experienced occasional shooting ear pain and difficulty wearing earrings since your surgery. Can you describe exactly where in your ear the pain occurs and what triggers it?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient has a history of polycystic ovarian syndrome, depression, and chronic bilateral ear infections. She underwent right ear tympanoplasty 12 weeks ago. Although audiology report from one week ago showed improved hearing by 20 decibels, she reports occasional shooting pain when eating and discomfort when wearing earrings. She describes her job as stressful and mentions poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that history; the shooting pain while eating and discomfort with earrings are concerning for a specific complication after your tympanoplasty. Given your history of chronic infections and the timing, are you experiencing any discharge, fullness, or tinnitus in the right ear? REQUEST IMAGES: Right ear otoscopy.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Occasional shooting pain in the ear with eating. I also have Discomfort when wearing earrings, Stress from job, Poor sleep quality. To keep my notes clear, please give only one final answer and keep it to a single direct conclusion.

speaker: Doctor
text: The shooting pain when eating suggests irritation of the auriculotemporal nerve, and the discomfort with earrings points to the anterior crura of the tympanic membrane. Have you noticed any visible granulation tissue or a small skin tag (skin tag) protruding from your ear canal near the eardrum? REQUEST IMAGES: Right ear otoscopy.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: History of polycystic ovarian syndrome, depression, and chronic bilateral ear infections. Underwent right ear tympanoplasty 12 weeks prior. Social history: Works as a cashier at a local department store.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Auricular Granuloma (Chondrodermatitis Nodularis Helicis of the Ear Canal)
